images.title: 36 has a factor that pairs with itself
images.purpose: Shows the five factor pairs of 36, where the last pair is 6 with itself, so 36 has 9 factors, an odd number.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Five pill shaped cards stacked one above the other in the centre, with one short tag to their right.
images.exact_structure: Exactly 5 horizontal pill shaped cards of equal size stacked vertically with even spacing. Each card is split down the middle into a left half and a right half. Cards 1 to 4 from the top read 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12 and 4 × 9; on each, the left half is filled teal (#0072B2) and the right half amber (#E69F00), showing two different partner factors. Card 5 at the bottom reads 6 × 6, both halves filled reddish purple (#CC79A7), and a small curved reddish purple arrow loops from its left half back to its right half to show 6 is its own partner. To the right of the stack, a short dark brace spans all 5 cards and is tagged 9 factors. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: A square number has one factor that pairs with itself, so its factor count is odd.
images.description: Shows the five factor pairs of 36, where the last pair is 6 with itself, so 36 has 9 factors, an odd number.

image_decisions.why: Seeing 6 × 6 as the one pair without a different partner explains why squares have an odd number of factors.
